concepts.preferred_label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
concepts.why: Patient has NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (<25%)
Patient has elevated brain natriuretic peptide and NYHA stage III heart failure
Patient has alternating QRS complex morphologies and delta wave present in QRS complex B
Patient has bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema
Patient has left ventricular ejection fraction <25% and global hypokinesis
Elevated troponin levels indicate myocardial injury, which is a key feature of acute coronary syndrome.

rationales.F01: Bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema is a common presentation of fluid overload, which is often associated with heart failure.
rationales.F05: The absence of acute cardiopulmonary processes on chest radiograph makes it less likely that the patient has an acute coronary syndrome or other cardiopulmonary condition.
rationales.F06: A left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 25% is a strong indicator of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
rationales.F09: Alternating QRS complex morphologies are a characteristic finding in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.
rationales.F11: An elevated brain natriuretic peptide level is a strong indicator of heart failure.
